summary.name: Platform as a service
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing Platform as a service (PaaS), a cloud model where users deploy and manage applications on a provider-managed platform without building the underlying infrastructure.
use_cases: understanding PaaS as a cloud service model
choosing between public, private and hybrid PaaS
hosting and deploying applications without managing servers
building real-time voice or messaging features via CPaaS
reviewing history of early PaaS offerings
summary.what_it_does: The page is a general encyclopedia entry explaining Platform as a service. It describes PaaS as a cloud model where the provider manages runtime, middleware, operating system, servers, storage and networking while the customer manages applications and data. It covers three delivery modes (public cloud, private behind a firewall, and software on IaaS) and notes related variants such as communications PaaS (CPaaS) and mobile PaaS (mPaaS). It also gives a brief history, including Zimki as an early public PaaS launched by Fotango in 2006.
notable: Explains public, private and hybrid PaaS deployment models
Covers CPaaS and mobile PaaS variants
History of Zimki, an early PaaS that closed and was not open-sourced
Notes the UK GOV.UK PaaS was decommissioned after running from 2015 to 2023
caveats: Listed on awesome-selfhosted as PaaS management software, but the page itself is a general concept article and not a specific tool
Disadvantages cited include increased pricing at scale, reduced control and lack of operational features
PaaS providers may restrict supported software, languages and interfaces
